title: Canonical evaluated norm-algebraic-closure bar augmentation for finite-rank actions
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, an integer $d\geq0$, and a profinite group $G$ (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected). Let $\rho:G\to\mathrm{GL}_d(E)$ define a jointly continuous linear action on $E^d$. Put $B(S)=C(S,\Omega)$ on the small coherent profinite site [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $N=B^d$, with the internal $G$-action given by $\rho$ extended to $B$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use ordinary derived categories and ordinary total right derived invariants $R\Gamma_G$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories, lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar]. Let $\operatorname{ev}_*$ evaluate at the one-point profinite set and forget scalars.

Define the nonnegative cochain complex $U_B^\bullet$ of internal $B$-modules by $U_B^n(S)=C(S\times G^n,\Omega^d)$ and
$$(df)(s;g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=\rho(g_1)f(s;g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^n(-1)^af(s;g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(s;g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
For $n=0$ this is $dv(s;g)=\rho(g)v(s)-v(s)$. Write $B[\underline G^n]$ for the free internal module. Evaluation identifies $U_B^n$ with the underived internal Hom from $B[\underline G^n]$ to $N$. Its canonical resolution comparisons into the derived internal Homs, using compatible nonnegative resolutions, define an augmentation from $U_B^\bullet$ to the derived bar totalization. Compose its localization with the inverse of the evaluation-normalized bar isomorphism of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] and apply $\operatorname{ev}_*$. This specifies a morphism
$$j_{B,\rho}:Q(C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\Omega^d))\longrightarrow\operatorname{ev}_*R\Gamma_G(N[0])$$
in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, where $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,\Omega^d)=U_B^\bullet(*)$ and $Q$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The morphism $j_{B,\rho}$ is an isomorphism. Its specification is independent of compatible resolution choices, is natural in continuous $E$-linear equivariant maps of finite-dimensional representations, and has degree-zero normalization equal to the inclusion of invariant vectors. No assertion that each individual $U_B^n\to R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(B[\underline G^n],N[0])$ is invertible is included. The coefficient field remains the incomplete norm-topological $\Omega$; all its continuous functions are retained.

proof.text: Choose one nonnegative equivariant injective resolution $N\to I^\bullet$ and its compatible bar double complex. By [lem-sfb-profinite-free-hom-resolution-evaluation], its evaluation has terms $D^{p,q}=I^q(G^p)$ with the same augmentation and restriction maps. In resolution degree zero, left exactness gives $\ker d_v=N(G^p)=C(G^p,\Omega^d)$; the cofaces are exactly those in the item. Evaluation at $*$ is exact by [lem-zl-contractible-derived-sections-tensor], since the point is extremally disconnected, so it takes the internal bar total to this finite-diagonal total.

source.place: Paragraph (3), evaluated norm-coefficient bar comparison, agent expansion

proof.text: For $q>0$, take a horizontal cocycle $x$ of the vertical-cohomology row. By [lem-sfb-evaluated-positive-bar-row-local-effacement], its class restricts to zero for an open subgroup $H$. Apply [lem-sfb-evaluated-positive-bar-row-transfer]: $[G:H][x]=\operatorname{cor}\operatorname{res}[x]=0$. The index is a positive integer and the row cohomology is a $\mathbf Q$-vector space, so $[x]=0$. This proves $H_h^pH_v^q(D)=0$ for every $p\geq0,q>0$; it does not prove columnwise acyclicity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), evaluated norm-coefficient bar comparison, agent expansion

proof.text: Apply [thm-sp-double-complex-spectral-sequences] to $D$: $E_1^{p,q}=H_v^q(D^{p,\bullet})$, $E_2^{p,q}=H_h^pH_v^q(D)$, with finite filtration and convergence in every total degree. By [lem-weil-pbc-first-quadrant-row-collapse], step 2 makes the edge $H^n(C_{\mathrm{cts}}^\bullet)\to H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ an isomorphism. This edge is induced by the actual map $C^p_{\mathrm{cts}}=\ker d_v^{p,0}\hookrightarrow D^{p,0}$, hence is the resolution augmentation, not an unspecified cohomological identification. Its localization is an isomorphism by the definition of the derived category.

source.place: Paragraph (3), evaluated norm-coefficient bar comparison, agent expansion

proof.text: Compose this localized augmentation with the inverse of the normalized bar isomorphism of [lem-sfb-condensed-derived-invariant-bar] and evaluate. These are precisely the operations specifying $j_{B,\rho}$, so $j_{B,\rho}$ is invertible. For any equivariant coefficient map choose a chain lift between resolutions. Postcomposition commutes with each map from the underived Hom, so the augmentation square commutes. [lem-sfb-condensed-bar-total-naturality] identifies all such lifts and changes of resolution after localization, giving the required independence and naturality.

source.place: Paragraph (3), evaluated norm-coefficient bar comparison, agent expansion

proof.text: The degree-zero kernel is $\{v\in\Omega^d:\rho(g)v=v\text{ for every }g\in G\}$. The comparison sends such a vector through $N\to I^0$ in bar degree zero. The normalized bar augmentation identifies its inverse image with that same invariant vector, yielding the invariant-inclusion normalization. Rank zero gives zero complexes; for $G=1$ the usual alternating constant complex has degree-zero cohomology $\Omega^d$ and vanishes above zero. Every construction used the unchanged all-continuous coefficient sheaf $B$.

split_report.summary: Kept the original statement and actual normalized augmentation. Separated finite-coset transfer on vertical-cohomology rows and noncomplete norm-coefficient local effacement; combined them by rational index cancellation, then used the first-quadrant spectral sequence. Did not use the false global Omega-valued Cech exactness or the finite complete-field column lemma.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact section evaluation on the extremally disconnected one-point profinite set.
Generic finite-diagonal first-quadrant spectral sequence and its functorial convergence.
Generic edge isomorphism when positive rows vanish; no different geometric route is substituted.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q69-6935ff5b9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, all cited statements and the parent's use of the item; statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, proof_deps equals the union of uses, and no SGA source is used. Step 1 (evaluation of D at the point, with ker d_v^{p,0}=C(G^p,Omega^d)), step 3 (Stacks 0130/0132 spectral sequence plus row collapse, the edge being the actual augmentation), step 4 (bar-total-naturality) and step 5 (G=1 complex has d=0 in even degrees and id in odd degrees, rank 0 is zero) are correct. The transfer node is a generic finite-coset construction, true, and not covered by lem-sfb-continuous-cochain-finite-index-transfer or the split-coset induction node. The local-effacement node: p=0 is vacuous and finite G works with H=1. At p=1 a coset translation argument (lambda_g^* x = g·x|_H) shows it is exactly E_2^{1,q}=0, so the open subgroup adds nothing there. For G=Z_l with trivial action it is equivalent to the item's own H^2 claim, using Q'=C(-,Omega)/C_fin. So it is not a restatement of the item and not stronger than it in the base case, but it carries the whole analytic content and its reference is WANTED: I could neither prove nor refute it. Positive E_1 entries do exist (H^1(Z_l,Omega) is nonzero by the Cech counterexample). Maintainer note: lem-sfb-evaluated-positive-bar-row-local-effacement is the item's open analytic core. tool_uses accepted: contractible evaluation, double-complex spectral sequences, row collapse.
